name: identity_token_stable
description: This install's identity for servers (design 6.12): a device key of 16 random bytes made on the first launch and kept in user://net.cfg; read again it is the same, and the first name is generated from it. The key never leaves the device: every connection sends HMAC-SHA1(key, 'Groundhold identity v1\n' + origin)[:16] in HELLO (the hub's session and a --join match alike), the same token for one server, another for every other, never the key, never in a URL. The origin is normalised as the server's identity.origin() does, and the README's reference vectors hold. The key is random by design, so --determinism runs this once.

steps.msg: 16 bytes, made on the first launch
and read back from disk: stable per install
kept in user://net.cfg, where M1 kept it
the first name comes from it, until the player confirms one
origins normalised as the server reads them: case, trailing dot, IPv6 brackets, default ports, ws and wss apart

steps.assert: I.token_for('ws://host/causeway', ref) != I.token_for('wss://host/causeway', ref) and I.token_for('wss://host/causeway', ref) == I.token_for('wss://HOST:443/other', ref)
steps.msg: one token per origin, a plaintext server never gets a TLS server's
HELLO to 192.168.1.20 carried a token, not the device key
the token for that server's origin (the fake sequencer echoes it as the identity)
a --join match on the same server sends the same token

steps.assert: second != first and second != key and second == I.token_for('ws://192.168.1.21:8766/causeway')
steps.msg: the next server gets its own token: unlinkable across servers
and the first server the same token again: stable per origin
